title: /collection fixed topbar overlaps table headers after spacer trim
description: Followup to pokedumpster-ldy: I trimmed topbarSpacer from 5.5rem to 4.4rem in pursuit of removing the gap above table headers, but 4.4rem is shorter than the actual rendered topbar (≈5.3rem with the two rows + paddings + border) so the fixed bar now covers the top of the table. Switch the topbar from position:fixed to position:sticky and drop the spacer entirely — sticky naturally takes its own height in the flow, so no measure-and-match is needed. The original 'fixed prevents horizontal table scroll dragging the bar off-left' concern doesn't apply because .tableScroll handles horizontal overflow within itself; the page never scrolls horizontally.

title: 'All cards' toggle should use the exact existing collection format, mixing owned + unowned
description:
Current implementation built a separate catalog grid and a separate catalog table when 'All cards' is on. Wrong intent — the user wants the same grid/table format as the owned collection view, with unowned cards mixed in (dimmed via .missing) alongside owned ones.

Work:
1. Extend CatalogSearchRow with the fields the existing table needs (supertype, subtypes, types, attacks, set_ptcgo_code, set_symbol_url) so a catalog row can render the Class/Type/Cost/Set columns.
2. Frontend: when allCards is on, synthesize 'unowned' rows from catalog matches that the user doesn't already own, and merge them into the same arrays the existing grid (filtered) and table (sorted) iterate over. Render them with the same UI; .missing class dims them.
3. Click on unowned tile/row opens the existing CardModal so the user picks a variant and adds copies via the stepper. After close, reload so the row flips to its real owned state.
4. Remove the separate catalog branches I added — one unified rendering path.

title: Card modal/detail: combat data on right of art (wide viewports) + stepper-style add
description:
Two related card-detail UX changes:

1. **Layout**: Today abilities, attacks, and weakness/resistance/retreat render in full-width sections BELOW the card art on every viewport. On wide viewports they should sit to the RIGHT of the art, in the same column as the existing metadata (name, type, HP, element, etc.). On narrow viewports keep the current stacked layout.

2. **Stepper add**: The Printings table has a single '+ Add' button per variant. Replace with the [- N +] stepper VariantModal already uses on /browse, so the user can add or remove a copy without going through the per-copy table. Use deleteCopyByPrinting for the '-' button (already in api.ts). Drop the now-redundant 'Owned' column (count lives in the stepper). Filter deprecated printings out of the table unless the user owns a copy (mirror the VariantModal filter we shipped in pokedumpster-jmn).
close_reason: Closed

title: Global card-search toggle on collection page (add cards you don't own)
description:
Today the /collection search bar only filters the user's owned copies. To add a card you don't yet own, you have to navigate to the right set in /browse and click through the binder. Add an 'All cards (catalog)' toggle next to the existing search box; when on, the search matches against the full catalog. Unowned matches render as new rows in the results list with an inline '+ Add' affordance that opens the existing VariantModal scoped to that card. Owned matches keep their current presentation.

Backend: GET /api/cards/catalog?q=... returns lightweight rows (card_id, set_code, number, name, image_small, owned_count) for fuzzy name/set/number matches across pkdump.cards. owned_count makes it cheap for the frontend to distinguish unowned-but-found from owned.

Frontend: collection page wires the toggle; when on, fetches the catalog endpoint instead of (or in addition to) filtering the owned list. Click +Add → reuse VariantModal (needs a slot-shaped fetch — either reuse /api/card/{set}/{number} or extend the catalog endpoint to include printings on demand).
notes: UI note: unowned rows must use the same greyed-out 'missing' visual treatment that browse/[set] applies to unowned binder slots (class:missing), so a mixed result set is visually parseable at a glance.
close_reason: Closed

title: link_card_printings flattens multi-product-per-card pricing
description:
tcgcsv::link_card_printings runs UPDATE printings SET tcgplayer_product_id = ?1 WHERE card_id = ?2 — so all variants of a card end up pointing to the SAME TCGplayer product, whichever the linker processed last. TCGplayer actually has separate products per pattern (Holo vs Reverse Holo vs Poke Ball vs Master Ball vs Trainer Gallery), each with its own pricing. Today, pokeball_rh and masterball_rh printings for 151 / Prismatic Evolutions share the price (and the new card-detail price-history chart) of the base printing, not their actual market.

Fix scope:
1. Match TCGplayer products to a specific printing variant, not just to a card. TCGplayer's extendedData typically carries hints (e.g. 'Number' with a suffix, or product name containing 'Master Ball'). Need to parse those and route to the right printing_id.
2. Schema is already OK — printings.tcgplayer_product_id is per-printing — just the linker logic is too coarse.
3. After the fix, re-run 'pkdump data refresh' to relink.

Order-of-operations matters: should land before any user-facing UI that promises per-pattern pricing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bogus reverse_holo printings on pre-Legendary-Collection sets (base1…base5)
description: Reverse holos didn't exist in the English Pokémon TCG until Legendary Collection (base6, 2002-05-24). But for Common/Uncommon/Rare cards in the original base, jungle, fossil, etc. sets, pokemontcg.io has no TCGplayer price-key block, so layer-1 expansion (variants_from_price_keys) yields nothing and layer-2 (bootstrap_from_rarity) kicks in. The bootstrap unconditionally adds 'reverse_holo' for those rarities, so the browse 'Add' modal shows a non-existent reverse-holo variant for, e.g., base1-58.\n\nFix: pass each card's set release_date into the expansion and have bootstrap_from_rarity skip reverse_holo when release_date < 2002-05-24. Threads through expand_variants → expand_all_printings (which already SELECTs from cards — just JOIN sets). Then re-run 'pkdump data refresh' on prod to soft-deprecate the wrong rows. Also filter deprecated printings out of the browse modal unless the user owns a copy, so existing wrong printings disappear from the UI.
close_reason: Closed

title: Card-detail price history chart (time-series graph)
description:
Card-detail view currently shows only the latest market price per printing (CardDetailView.svelte 'Printings' table → Market column). User wants a time-series chart of price over time per printing.

Data is already there: prices table has rows keyed on (tcgplayer_product_id, sub_type_name, source, price_type, observed_at), one snapshot per day per (printing, finish, price_type). pkdump-refresh@<instance>.timer pulls daily at 06:00 UTC via 'pkdump data refresh' → import_tcgcsv → import_prices with observed_at = today's UTC date. INSERT OR IGNORE makes same-day reruns no-ops.

Scope for v1:
- New API endpoint: GET /api/card/{set}/{number}/prices → series per printing × price_type (default: market). Returns [{printing_id, sub_type_name, price_type, points: [{date, price}, …]}].
- Frontend: small chart (sparkline or full chart — pick one) under the Printings table. One line per printing, showing 'market' by default; toggle for low/mid/high/directLow optional.
- Reasonable default window (90d? all-time?). Decide as part of design.

Future v2 (depends on pokedumpster-ayh per-condition price history): overlay condition-adjusted series.

Open question: chart lib — Chart.js, ECharts, or plain SVG? Stay light; the rest of the app has no chart dep yet.
close_reason: Closed

title: Containerfile uses short image names; podman build fails for rust:1.94-slim
description: podman's shortnames.conf aliases 'node' and 'debian' to docker.io/library/* but not 'rust'. With no unqualified-search-registries configured, 'podman build' of the prod image dies on 'FROM rust:1.94-slim'. Fully-qualify the three FROM lines (docker.io/library/...) — portable across machines and recommended by podman docs.
close_reason: Closed

title: pkmn.gg userscript: API recon — collection-page network shape
description: Initial pkmngg_export.user.js finds nothing on the live site. Need a sample of pkmn.gg's authenticated collection API: the request URL pattern, response shape, pagination model. User to capture via DevTools Network panel; then add a recognised path + parser branch.
notes:
Recon attempt against me@ryangantt.com:

- NextAuth magic-link callback https://pkmn.gg/api/auth/callback/email?token=…
  redirects to /auth/email-confirm which requires a form button click to
  consume the token (handled in scripts/pkmngg_fetch.js).
- After confirm we get a refresh_token cookie. /pkmn/v1/auth/me returns
  {id, email, name, emailVerified:true, profile:null, roles:[],
   areWritesLocked:false} → SPA gates every route behind /auth/newuser
  (the "Welcome! Choose Your Username" page).
- API host is api.tcg.gg/pkmn/v1/…; nav shell exposes /collections + /lists.
- Magic-link identity is separate from OAuth in NextAuth by default —
  almost certainly why this signed us into an empty shadow account
  rather than the user's real OAuth-linked collection.

Next path if revisiting:
- Storage-state export from a logged-in browser
  (`scripts/pkmngg_fetch.js` will reuse any storage_state.json).
- Or wait for pkmn.gg to ship account-linking by verified email.

title: /collection fixes didn't take: main padding override loses specificity, Qty header sets column width
description:
Followup to pokedumpster-bp7. Two of the four fixes shipped but had no visible effect:

1. :global(body main) { padding: 0 } in collection/+page.svelte loses the specificity war against the layout's scoped main { padding: 1.5rem } (svelte hashes main → .s-XXX main, specificity (0,1,1); my body main is (0,0,2)). Layout still wins. Use !important or move the override.

2. table.dd .qty width: 2.5rem is set on the td but the th for Qty has only class 'num', so the column width is dictated by the header (text + padding + sort caret). Add 'qty' to the th's extra class via the sortable snippet so the width applies to both.
close_reason: Closed

title: /collection space-economy: edge-to-edge content, tighten gaps, Qty width, price box
description:
Four small but compounding wins on the collection page:

1. Global main padding (1.5rem L/R) is wasted on /collection — the page has its own sticky chrome and the table/grid should run edge-to-edge.
2. table.dd has margin-top: 0.8rem and .cardgrid has margin-top: 0.8rem, plus topbarSpacer height: 5.5rem — these stack into a visible gap between the bottom of the fixed topbar and the first row of results.
3. Qty column has no explicit width and inherits th/td padding for a value that's almost always 1-2 chars. Shrink to a small fixed width.
4. Rename the 'Market' column to 'Price'; wrap each price value in a DD-style pill (dark bg + thin border + small padding) so it reads as a tagged value.

title: Pre-LC variants: 1st Edition, Shadowless, Wizards-promo holo/non-holo not modelled
description:
After the reverse_holo cutoff fix (pokedumpster-jmn) the pre-LC era still has variant gaps:

1. 1st Edition vs Unlimited — base1..base5 + gym1/gym2 + neo1..neo4 all shipped in 1st Edition and Unlimited print runs. KNOWN_VARIANTS already has first_ed_holo / first_ed_normal / unlimited_holo, but layer-1 needs pokemontcg.io price-key support (1stEditionHolofoil / 1stEditionNormal / unlimitedHolofoil) AND/OR overlay rules per set+rarity.

2. Shadowless (Base Set first print) — not in KNOWN_VARIANTS at all. Add a 'shadowless_holo' / 'shadowless_normal' code and overlay rules for base1.

3. Wizards Black Star Promos (basep) — current bootstrap assigns 'Promo' rarity → ['holo'] for all 53 cards, but real basep is a mix (e.g. #1 Pikachu is non-holo, #4 Mewtwo is holo). Either thread a rarity-bootstrap-doesn't-fit special case, or write per-card overlays in variant_augmentations.json keyed by set='basep'+number. Probably overlay is the lowest-friction path.

None of these block anyone today — pkdump has no users tracking pre-LC cards. File so the audit history is here when someone does.

title: Pattern-variant overlays missing for ASC, BLK, WHT
description:
Three modern sets currently fall back to the rarity bootstrap (normal/reverse_holo/holo) but very likely have pattern-variant printings the way 151 and Prismatic Evolutions do:

- me2pt5 (ASC / Ascended Heroes, 2026-01-30) — TCGCSV publishes Normal+RH+Holofoil
- zsv10pt5 (BLK / Black Bolt, 2025-07-18) — TCGCSV publishes Holofoil only (same shape as PRE)
- rsv10pt5 (WHT / White Flare, 2025-07-18) — Holofoil only (same as PRE)

For BLK/WHT the Holofoil-only TCGCSV signal matches sv8pt5's, which is the tell that pattern variants exist outside the base TCGplayer product. For ASC the bootstrap might already be right, or there may be additional pattern printings.

Action: identify the actual pattern variant names (energy / poke ball / master ball / etc. — needs authoritative reference, probably Bulbapedia or the official set release notes), then add overlay rules in data/overrides/variant_augmentations.json keyed by set + rarity. Pattern: clone the existing sv3pt5/sv8pt5 rules and adjust the 'add' list.

title: Per-condition price history (NM vs LP vs MP vs HP vs DMG)
description:
Current prices table has ONE history per (tcgplayer_product_id, sub_type_name, source, price_type, observed_at) — sub_type is finish (Normal/Holo/RH), not condition. NM and LP copies of the same printing share the same chart, which doesn't reflect resale reality. User wants distinct price streams per condition.

Blocked on data sourcing: TCGCSV publishes one market price per product (effectively NM). Need to choose:
  (a) heuristic multipliers on NM (LP ≈ 0.85×, MP ≈ 0.6×, HP ≈ 0.4×, DMG ≈ 0.25×) — cheap, lossy
  (b) per-condition listings from eBay sold / TCGplayer conditional pricing — accurate, more infra

Schema impact when shipped: add a 'condition' column to prices (or a sibling table prices_by_condition), and a UNIQUE that includes it. Likely keep the NM stream + add multiplier-derived rows for other conditions in v1, then swap to real data in v2 when (b) is built.
notes: Deferred from v1 chart build (2026-05-23): user chose 'NM only, no multipliers' so there is no v1 code change. Pick this up once a real per-condition price source is chosen (eBay sold, TCGplayer conditional, or otherwise). Schema/API design notes already in the issue description.
